stem:
Yash keeps the four numbers 2, 3, 4 and 5 fixed. He only changes the + and − signs between them, writing expressions of the form 2 ± 3 ± 4 ± 5.

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: Changing one sign can flip the parity of the value.
Every such value has the same parity.
Changing the + and − signs cannot change the parity of the value.
The common parity depends on a sign written before the first number 2.

teacher.key_rationale: Flipping a sign changes the total by twice an integer, so parity is preserved. Every 2±3±4±5 value shares one parity. Claiming a flip of parity reverses that. Putting the decision on a sign before 2 over-scopes the idea.
